title: Same coin, 2,000 steps. Line: 207 of 10,000 walkers still out. Plane: 3,013.
description:
Ten thousand walkers start at home on a line and step left or right by one unit each turn. Ten thousand walkers start at home on a plane and step north, south, east or west by one unit each turn. Both groups take 2,000 steps from seed 0 (one seeded stream per world, numpy RandomState). A walker counts as home once it has stood on the origin again at any step after the first. Green cells and bars are walkers that have been home; gold ones have not.

Measured at seed 0:
- line: home at least once by step 2: 5,053 of 10,000 (50.5%); by step 10: 7,530; by step 100: 9,178 (91.8%); by step 1,000: 9,716 (97.2%); by step 2,000: 9,793 (97.9%), so 207 still out
- plane: home at least once by step 2: 2,480 (24.8%); by step 10: 4,182; by step 100: 5,822 (58.2%); by step 1,000: 6,771 (67.7%); by step 2,000: 6,987 (69.9%), so 3,013 still out, 14.6 times as many as on the line
- of the walkers that got home, the median first return is step 2 on the line and step 6 on the plane; the 90th percentile is step 48 on the line and step 274 on the plane
- check on the line: the exact chance of no return by step 2,000 is 1.78%; the seeded run gives 2.07%, and an independent 100,000-walker run at seed 1 gives 1.80%
- context, not narrated: on a cubic lattice (three dimensions) 3,335 of 10,000 are home by step 2,000 and the count has almost stopped growing (3,308 at step 1,000)

Why: on the line and on the plane every walker returns home eventually (Polya, 1921), but the plane takes far longer: the share still out falls like one over the square root of the step count on the line and only like one over the logarithm on the plane. In three dimensions about a third ever return.

The numbers in the narration are the printed outputs of this exact run.

Made end to end by an AI agent: simulation, footage, voice, music, and edit.
